Inflation ticked up to 4.5% in September 📈

Stats SA says prices were 4.5% higher than a year ago, up from 4.4% in August.

The biggest push came from:
🚗 Transport: up 10.8% (petrol and diesel)
🏠 Housing and utilities: up 5.2% (rent, electricity, water)

What it means for you: if your salary went up by less than 4.5% this year, your money buys less than it did last year.

The next inflation figure comes out on 18 November.

The Medium-Term Budget in 60 seconds 🇿🇦

On 21 October Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana tabled the Medium-Term Budget. Here's what matters for your household:

⛽ Fuel levy cut from Wednesday 4 November: R1.50/litre off petrol and R3/litre off diesel until 1 December. Then R1 (petrol) and R1.50 (diesel) off until 5 January 2027.
📉 Growth forecast for 2026 cut to 1.2%, down from 1.6% in February.
💸 Treasury says government debt has stabilised and is starting to fall.
🏥 Extra money for health, education, municipalities and the fight against gender-based violence.

The fuel relief costs about R10 billion. Is it enough? Tell us below 👇

What the latest rate hike means for your bond 🏠

On 23 September the Reserve Bank raised the repo rate by 0.25% to 7.25%. Banks followed, so the prime lending rate is now 10.75%.

(Repo rate = what the Reserve Bank charges banks. Prime = what banks charge their best customers. Most home loans, car loans and credit cards follow prime.)

On a R1 million home loan over 20 years at prime:
• January (prime 10.25%): about R9,816 a month
• Now (prime 10.75%): about R10,152 a month

That's roughly R336 more every month, from two small hikes this year.

Why? The Reserve Bank is worried fuel prices will push inflation above 5% in the coming months.

Why a war far away hits your wallet in Mzansi 🌍➡️🇿🇦

1️⃣ Tension in the Middle East, around the Strait of Hormuz, disrupts oil supply.
2️⃣ Oil prices rise (close to $100 a barrel).
3️⃣ South Africa imports its fuel and pays in dollars, and the rand has been weak.
4️⃣ Petrol and diesel go up.
5️⃣ Trucks carry our food, so groceries go up too.
6️⃣ Inflation rises, so the Reserve Bank raises interest rates.
7️⃣ Your bond, car payment and credit card cost more.

That's how one event overseas ends up in your monthly budget.

text:
3 money moves for November 💡

Fuel, interest rates and inflation are all up. Here are 3 things worth checking this month:

1️⃣ Find out which of your debts follow prime. Bonds, car loans, credit cards and store cards usually do. Every rate hike makes them more expensive.
2️⃣ If you have spare cash, paying extra on your most expensive debt (often credit and store cards) usually beats leaving it in a savings account.
3️⃣ Plan for December now. The fuel levy relief gets smaller from 2 December, and January is long. Put aside a little from each pay this month.

Petrol price: what to expect on Wednesday 4 November ⛽

October already set a record: R30.25 a litre for 95 inland.

The latest forecasts point to another increase in November, of roughly R1.50 to R2.30 a litre for petrol, because oil is high and the rand is weak. These are forecasts: the official price is announced just before Wednesday.

The good news: the fuel levy cut from the Medium-Term Budget starts the same day, taking R1.50 a litre off petrol and R3 off diesel. That softens the blow.

💡 If an increase is confirmed, filling up before Wednesday helps.

Is the prime rate on its way out? 🏦

Most South African loans (bonds, car finance, credit cards) are priced as "prime plus" or "prime minus". Prime is 10.75% right now, which is 3.5% above the Reserve Bank's repo rate.

The Reserve Bank has proposed that consumer loans be priced off the repo rate itself instead. It's linked to the retirement of JIBAR, an old benchmark interest rate that ends on 31 December 2026.

What it could mean for you: your loan might be quoted as "repo + 3.5%" instead of "prime". The label changes, but what matters is the total rate in your agreement. Always check that number on any new loan.

This is a proposal, not a law yet. We'll keep you posted.
